changelog: Restore token usage and cost tracking for streamed Together AI responses by patching the pinned @ai-sdk/togetherai SDK so its chat models request stream_options.include_usage.
details: Root cause: @ai-sdk/togetherai@2.0.41 builds its chat model via `new OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel(modelId, getCommonModelConfig('chat'))`, and getCommonModelConfig returns only {provider, url, headers, fetch} - it never forwards includeUsage. @ai-sdk/openai-compatible only emits `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` when config.includeUsage is truthy, so Together AI never returned the final usage chunk, the AI SDK resolved usage as all-undefined, and the session pipeline (processor.ts `value.usage ?? new Usage({})`) silently persisted zeros; cost was $0 because cost is price x token counts. Kilo's own provider layer cannot compensate: the SDK's TogetherAIProviderSettings has no includeUsage field and unknown options are dropped - proven empirically with a mock-fetch probe (passing includeUsage:true left the request body unchanged). Fix: a Bun patchedDependencies patch on the pinned @ai-sdk/togetherai@2.0.41 that constructs the chat model with `{ ...getCommonModelConfig('chat'), includeUsage: true }`, registered in root package.json and bun.lock (1-line lockfile delta). This single SDK-level change covers both the opencode provider path (packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:154) and the migrated core plugin path (packages/core/src/plugin/provider/togetherai.ts:11) with no provider source file modified. Two layers of hermetic regression tests added (SDK level: provider/chatModel/languageModel routes plus a non-streaming guard; core plugin level: togetherai and custom-togetherai provider IDs); the mocks only emit a usage chunk when stream_options.include_usage is present, so the tests verifiably fail without the patch. Also fixed a pre-existing module-init cycle failure in packages/core/test/plugin/provider-togetherai.test.ts via the repo-standard provider registry import. Verification: 4+5+23 unit tests pass, negative check (patch reverted) turns them red as expected, both packages typecheck clean, oxlint findings identical to the HEAD baseline, prettier/annotation/CI-scheduling guards pass, and the CLI builds successfully with pinned Bun 1.4.4 + Zig 0.14.4 (version, models-snapshot and sandbox-worker smoke tests pass) with the patched provider confirmed in the bundled source map. Two reviewer rounds returned pass_with_comment with no blocking issues; the 1 should-fix and 4 nit/P1/P2 findings were all addressed and re-verified.

failed_points: Mock-fetch probe against the installed unpatched SDK: outgoing Together AI chat request body was {model, messages, stream:true} with NO stream_options, and the finish part carried usage {inputTokens:{}, outputTokens:{}}
Same probe with includeUsage:true passed into createTogetherAI: request body unchanged and usage still empty - empirically refutes the 'just set the provider option' remedy

Negative control: with the patch reverted in the installed store copy, packages/opencode/test/kilocode/together-usage.test.ts failed 3/4 and packages/core/test/plugin/provider-togetherai.test.ts failed 1/5 (expected red), then the patch was restored and both went green again

review_rounds.comments: No blocking issues. Patch applies cleanly to pristine @ai-sdk/togetherai@2.0.41, is scoped to the chat model only, does not affect doGenerate, and both consumption paths (opencode provider + core plugin) are covered. Should-fix: the dependency patch recorded no rationale for patching instead of bumping the dependency - state that upstream shipped an equivalent fix in 2.0.68 and the removal condition. Nits: the kilocode_change marker carried the same sentence twice, and the patch hunks lacked the `index <old>..<new> 100644` blob-hash lines used by the other files in patches/.

All round-1 fixes verified: the `#` comment block does not break Bun's or git's patch application, upstream 2.0.68 confirmed to contain the equivalent fix, the marker block still satisfies script/check-opencode-annotations.ts and the registry import is genuinely required (removing it reproduces the ReferenceError), and the three index blob hashes were independently recomputed and are correct. Regression sweep clean: patched-dependencies 23 pass, new tests pass and are genuine regressions, oxlint findings identical to the HEAD baseline, both packages typecheck clean, core suite 1399 pass / 1 pre-existing failure. Two remaining items, both addressed: P1 - the comment overstated the upstream 2.0.68 fix as 'the same fix' when upstream is a superset that also enables usage for completion models (comment reworded, and the removal condition now notes the behaviour difference); P2 - the new core test used it.live although it has no live OS behaviour and the rest of the file uses it.effect (switched to it.effect, 5 pass / 0 fail).
